clue.text: Look, and leave a trademark

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
to go is to leave or depart

explanation.surface: Someone is told to look about and then quit a brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is the emblem or symbol a company uses as its mark of identity.

clue.text: Man the Spanish woman leads inside the church

indicators.note: leads puts this piece in front of the others

parts.note: a lady is a woman
chap is informal for a man
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman guides a man into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a verb, to staff, but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lady Chapel is a chapel within a larger church, dedicated to the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: Holds fuel supplies must be cut for the not-so-young

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
older means less young

explanation.surface: Fuel stocks must be reduced for elderly people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds' is a verb in the surface but the definition describes a thing that holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasholder is a large tank, a gasometer, that stores town gas for distribution.

clue.text: See clue — prone, unfortunately, to rotundity

parts.note: the word see is pronounced like the letter C, a convention some setters use

indicators.note: something gone wrong unfortunately is out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, part of the pool of letters
taken as written, part of the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A cross-reference warns that someone lying around too much will grow fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' scrambles C (for 'See') with CLUE and PRONE. 'See clue' looks like a cross-reference instruction but is part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpulence is fatness or stoutness of body, the same as roundness of figure.

clue.text: On road crossing foreshore, whale is heading for the trees

indicators.note: heading puts the first piece at the front

parts.note: orc is an old name for a killer whale
a hard is a firm roadway or ramp over a beach for launching boats

explanation.surface: A whale on the shore road leads the way to some fruit trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hard' is a firm landing-place or slipway on a foreshore, a British coastal term.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plantation of fruit trees.

clue.text: Member with hat on interfered with vision

indicators.note: something interfered with is disturbed, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written, part of the pool of letters
taken as written, part of the pool of letters

explanation.surface: A politician's wearing a hat disrupted someone's line of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interfered with' scrambles MP, HAT and ON together.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is an apparition or ghostly sight seen by someone.

clue.text: Bovine merriment in the Cotswolds?

parts.note: a mooing cow is one that lows, so cattle laughing becomes a village name

explanation.walkthrough: A cow that 'lows' is a lower; the Cotswolds are hills in England with a village of this name.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a village in Gloucestershire in the Cotswold hills, read as the laughter of a mooing beast.

clue.text: Guiding principle is to number a letter

parts.note: en is the letter N spelt out

explanation.surface: A rule is to count each letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to number' looks like a verb; it is the abbreviation NUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A numen is a presiding divinity or spirit that guides a place or thing.

clue.text: Flier echoes merit

indicators.note: echoes means repeats the sound, so this is said aloud

parts.note: to merit something is to earn it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The erne is the sea eagle, a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Fruits for processing — crush the stones

indicators.note: food for processing is to be broken down and remade, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters
taken as written, part of the letters
taken as written, part of the letters

explanation.surface: Fruit bound for a factory has its pits crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for processing' scrambles CRUSH THE STONES. Conkers are the nuts of this tree.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the shiny brown nuts of the horse chestnut tree, conkers, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Historic ship not very suitable place for holding a dance

definitions.text: suitable place for holding a dance

indicators.note: not removes the following word from the ship's name

parts.note: Discovery was Captain Scott's Antarctic expedition ship, now preserved in Dundee
taken as written, the letters taken away

explanation.surface: A famous old vessel is judged a poor venue for a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' looks like a qualifier on 'suitable', but 'not' removes VERY from DISCOVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club or hall where people go to dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Not the tea lady

parts.note: char is slang for tea, so a woman named after it sounds like the one serving tea, but she is really a cleaner

explanation.walkthrough: 'char' is British slang for tea and also for a cleaning woman, so the obvious reading is denied.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a woman paid to clean houses or offices, not one who serves drinks.

clue.text: Zebra may have eaten elastic band once sported by gallant

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a zebra is a British pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes
a garter is an elastic band worn round the leg to hold up a stocking

explanation.surface: A striped animal has swallowed a rubber band, in a scene from an old play.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a striped British road crossing. Malvolio in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night appears cross-gartered, garters tied crosswise, to woo Olivia.
explanation.definitionFit: Garters crossed over the leg were a fashion worn by dandies in Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Idolatrise — comments in the press being misdirected

indicators.note: letters being misdirected are sent the wrong way and end up out of order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Newspaper opinion pieces that worship idols are misguided.
explanation.definitionFit: Editorials are leading articles expressing a newspaper's opinions.

clue.text: Tot leader held then cited as proof

indicators.note: one word held by another sits inside it

parts.note: to tot up is to add
Duce, Italian for leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: A child's head is gripped before being quoted as evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To adduce something is to bring it forward as evidence in an argument.

clue.text: Pink girl?

definitions.meaning: pink is a pale or gentle shade of red
a woman's first name, the question mark warning that it is one example

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the name gives a soft shade of red, which describes pink; whole, it is a female name.

clue.text: Muscle used in a game of chess?

definitions.meaning: a muscle that draws a body part back in

definitions.text: used in a game of chess?
definitions.meaning: a chess problem in which moves must be taken back

explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that pulls back, and also a type of chess puzzle in which moves are retracted.

clue.text: Serious listener, honestly not holy

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: not takes away the letters of the following word, in order, from the one before

parts.note: taken as written, the letters losing some
taken as written, the letters removed one by one

explanation.surface: A grave confessor hears things truthfully but without piety.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, O, L and Y in order from HONESTLY to leave NEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest describes someone sincere and grave in intent, the same as serious.

clue.text: Magnifying the sound of 19 across?

parts.note: the small bird sings in high chirps, so the device that amplifies high notes seems named for it

explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is the small bird; a loudspeaker for high frequencies is named after birdsong.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker that reproduces high frequencies.

clue.text: Lute-playing-a small piece-about to get the bird

indicators.note: about means round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a bit is a small piece of something

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played with and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A lutenist plays a short piece and is rewarded with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make the clue read like a concert programme, with 'the bird' as the reward; 'playing' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The blue tit is a small common European songbird with a blue cap.

clue.text: Shelters for those who run away

definitions.meaning: people who bunk off, British slang for running away

explanation.walkthrough: To 'do a bunk' or 'bunk off' is British slang for running away or skipping school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunkers are fortified refuges, and the word also names people who skip off.

clue.text: Flying fortress?

parts.note: suggests the wartime bomber, but means a stronghold floating in the sky, a fanciful dream

explanation.walkthrough: The Flying Fortress was an American bomber of the Second World War; here the fortress is literally up aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an impractical daydream or scheme with no foundation in reality.

clue.text: In the past, military force held the assembly place

parts.note: ago means in the past
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Long ago soldiers occupied the meeting ground.
explanation.walkthrough: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An agora was the open public square for gatherings in an ancient Greek city.

clue.text: National tax

definitions.meaning: a native of one particular country, here north of England
an old word for a payment or levy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Scot-free' originally meant free of paying a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scot is a native of Scotland, and scot was an old local tax.

clue.text: After the game Lawrence gets something to eat

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and hoops
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, is known by his initials

explanation.surface: Lawrence has a snack following a match on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence ('Lawrence of Arabia') gives his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small fried roll of minced food in breadcrumbs, eaten as a dish.

clue.text: Rate adjustment about ten above the norm

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the anagram goes round the other piece
an adjustment changes the arrangement of the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, the letters rearranged
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A tax rate is being changed by around ten per cent more than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjustment' turns RATE into ETRA, which goes 'about' X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional or beyond what is usual or expected.

clue.text: Stranger, taking a turn, gets ship to go off-course

indicators.note: a word taking a turn is twisted about, so its letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters rearranged
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A newcomer takes the helm and steers the vessel wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a turn' rearranges STRANGER to TRANSGRE. To transgress is literally to step beyond a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To transgress is to overstep a boundary or stray beyond what is permitted.

clue.text: His victim loses heart

parts.note: the god of love's arrow makes whoever it strikes give their heart away, not lose courage

explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' usually means becomes discouraged; here the victim falls in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, whose arrows made people fall for one another.
